tweets: NAD+ precursors and injections are often discussed without clear human data context. Many marketing claims skip over the actual evidence available. We're building a practice focused on transparent, evidence-forward peptide therapy.
Human data on NAD+ precursors is limited and mixed. The research that's out there points to uncertainty about effects and clinical relevance. This uncertainty guides our cautious clinical approach.

For NAD+ injections, human evidence is very sparse and preliminary. Most available data comes from small or uncontrolled studies, often industry-funded. Animal biology doesn't reliably translate to humans. We're designing care around this reality.

Our model routes patients to physician-supervised, 503A-compounded therapies with no research peptides. Labs and follow-up are included when clinically appropriate. This is not a refill mill but a clinical review process.

Compounded NAD+ therapies are not FDA-approved medications. Suitability is determined case-by-case by licensed clinicians. We avoid promising outcomes or guaranteed prescriptions, focusing instead on responsible, evidence-informed care.
